triage_metadata.task: Independent LLM path re-review of formal Augur Pass 1 Path Traversal SARIF codeFlows (ruleId py/augur/whoogle-search/pass1-path-traversal)
triage_metadata.independence_note: Triage verdicts below were derived exclusively from the SARIF codeFlows, labels/labels.json, report/query_generation_notes.md, and the real source tree under dataset/codeql_databases/path_traversal_dbs/whoogle-search_vuln. No PyVul ground truth, fix commits, or CVE descriptions were consulted for the per-finding verdicts. The ground-truth commit comparison is a separate section supplied at the operator's request after the independent triage and did not alter any verdict.
triage_metadata.scope_note: Only the 2 results carrying ruleId py/augur/whoogle-search/pass1-path-traversal were triaged. Diagnostics queries and CodeQL built-in security query suites were not present in pass1.sarif and none were counted.

findings.endpoint: PUT /config (route decorator app/routes.py:416, handlers @session_required @auth_required, function config() routes.py:419)

source.evidence: routes.py:426 `if 'name' in request.args:` -> routes.py:429 `request.args.get('name')` — direct flask request.args read; werkzeug percent-decodes once at parse time, no further decode on this chain

taint_flow.note: SARIF codeFlow step 0/1 — untrusted query param
SARIF codeFlow steps 2-3; os.path.join is taint-preserving: '..' segments survive, an absolute second argument replaces CONFIG_PATH entirely (label snk-240, summary tp 0.9)
SARIF codeFlow step 4; result assigned into session['config'] and returned to the client as JSON (routes.py:430-433)

sink.operation: arbitrary file READ (plus pickle deserialization of attacker-chosen file — secondary concern, CWE-502-adjacent)
sink.note: Not mere path concatenation: this is a genuine filesystem read whose loaded content is reflected to the attacker in the JSON response (routes.py:433).

escape_mechanisms: '..' segments: name=../../etc/foo survives os.path.join verbatim (join performs no normalization)
absolute path: name=/etc/foo — os.path.join discards CONFIG_PATH entirely when arg 2 is absolute
Windows drive letters (this db is analyzed on win32 host): name=C:/x/y replaces base
mixed/forward separators accepted by the underlying OS APIs

examined.reason: existence probe only — gates whether the load branch runs, performs no containment or canonicalization (check-then-open TOCTOU companion, not a barrier)
see preconditions — not a path-containment control, and bypassed in default credential-less deployments
business toggle (WHOOGLE_CONFIG_DISABLE, default false via read_config_bool app/utils/misc.py:18), not path validation

barriers.verified_absent: grep over app/routes.py confirms no normpath/realpath/resolve/relative_to/basename/'..'-rejection/regex-whitelist between source (429) and sink (430). The vulnerable version predates the fix's `os.path.normpath` + `^[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+$` regex (verified absent in this tree).
barriers.misdiagnosis_check: No Path.resolve/startsWith prefix check or login-only 'protection' was mistaken for containment — none exist on this chain; the empty isBarrier (MySanitizers.qll) is the accurate model.

preconditions: HTTP PUT (not GET) to /config with a 'name' query parameter
config_disabled must be false: app.config['CONFIG_DISABLE'] = read_config_bool('WHOOGLE_CONFIG_DISABLE') (routes.py:420-422, 425) — default false

auth_required (routes.py:48-74): if WHOOGLE_USER/WHOOGLE_PASS env vars are unset — the default for most self-hosted deployments — routes.py:64 `(not whoogle_user or not whoogle_pass)` short-circuits to `session['auth'] = True; return f(...)` with NO authentication; if credentials are configured, any validly authenticated user (single shared account) reaches the sink

for content exfiltration the target file must parse as a pickle (os.path.exists must also pass, routes.py:431, for the open to execute); non-pickle targets still permit existence probing and error differentiation

questions_1_to_10.1_source_attacker_controlled: yes — flask query parameter 'name', fully attacker-controlled string
questions_1_to_10.2_source_reaches_sink: yes — direct same-function flow, no async hop or wrapper: 429 -> join(427-429) -> open(430); SARIF codeFlows (both threadFlows) show exactly these nodes
questions_1_to_10.3_sink_is_sensitive_file_op: yes — open(...,'rb') + pickle.load, a real filesystem read with content reflected in the JSON response; not mere concatenation
questions_1_to_10.4_allowed_root_escape: yes — CONFIG_PATH (CONFIG_VOLUME or static/config) is the only intended root; '..' and absolute second-arg join semantics both escape it
questions_1_to_10.5_traversal_vectors_real: yes — no normalization exists at all, so '..', absolute paths, and separators all pass through unchanged; single framework-level percent-decode only
questions_1_to_10.6_containment_before_access: none — the only checks (os.path.exists) occur as TOCTOU companions, not pre-access containment
questions_1_to_10.7_barrier_misdiagnosis: none — no normpath/resolve/startsWith/auth-only false barrier was credited; empty barrier model is correct
questions_1_to_10.8_not_benign_static_serving: correct — this is an authenticated-user/credential-less-deployment arbitrary read outside the config root, not authorized static file serving, test code, or unreachable path
questions_1_to_10.9_overgeneralization_fp: no — source/sink shapes are the exact labeled sites (src-110, snk-242), path is the single documented full untrusted->path chain; database covers app/routes.py correctly (codeFlows carry real line numbers)
questions_1_to_10.10_cwe_mixing: no — single ruleId in SARIF, no diagnostics or builtin-suite results present

findings.rationale: Genuine CWE-22/23/36/73 arbitrary-file-read (with pickle deserialization side effect) on PUT /config: attacker-controlled query parameter joined under CONFIG_PATH with zero validation or canonicalization and opened directly. Reachable unauthenticated in default deployments (no WHOOGLE_USER/PASS) or by the shared authenticated account otherwise.

findings.endpoint: POST /config (route decorator app/routes.py:416, handlers @session_required @auth_required, function config() routes.py:419)

taint_flow.note: SARIF codeFlow step 0 — untrusted query param
SARIF codeFlow step 1; taint-preserving join (label snk-244, summary tp 0.9)
SARIF final step; open(...,'wb') creates/truncates the file; config_data = request.form.to_dict() (routes.py:437) is attacker-influenced content

sink.operation: arbitrary file CREATE/OVERWRITE (write) with attacker-influenced pickled-dict content
sink.note: Real filesystem write, not path construction; 'wb' truncates existing targets, enabling overwrite of arbitrary writable files.

escape_mechanisms: absolute path: name=/tmp/x replaces CONFIG_PATH entirely under os.path.join semantics
Windows drive letters and mixed separators on win32 hosts

note: CONFIG_PATH also holds whoogle.key (app/__init__.py:102) and the session dir (app/__init__.py:77-79) — escapes and in-root collisions both have security impact; overwrite of whoogle.key or session pickles is in-root but attacker-named

examined.reason: not path containment; bypassed entirely in default credential-less deployments (routes.py:64 short-circuit)
business toggle, default false, not path validation

barriers.verified_absent: no normpath/realpath/regex whitelist on this chain in the analyzed tree (pre-fix source); write happens immediately after the join with no probe at all (worse than the read side — not even an exists() TOCTOU companion)
barriers.misdiagnosis_check: No barrier over-crediting; MySanitizers empty barrier is accurate for this chain too.

preconditions: HTTP POST to /config with a 'name' query parameter and form body (config_data)
auth_required passable: default deployments with WHOOGLE_USER/WHOOGLE_PASS unset require NO authentication (routes.py:62-69); otherwise the single shared account
process write permissions on the target path (app typically runs with adequate perms in its container)

questions_1_to_10.1_source_attacker_controlled: yes — query parameter 'name', plus form-derived pickled content
questions_1_to_10.2_source_reaches_sink: yes — same-function direct flow 447 -> join(445-447) -> open 'wb'; both SARIF codeFlows show these exact nodes
questions_1_to_10.3_sink_is_sensitive_file_op: yes — open(...,'wb') + pickle.dump is a real create/overwrite write, not concatenation
questions_1_to_10.4_allowed_root_escape: yes — same join semantics; additionally in-root arbitrary-name writes (whoogle.key, session pickles) are impactful
questions_1_to_10.5_traversal_vectors_real: yes — zero normalization on the chain; '..'/absolute/separators all effective
questions_1_to_10.6_containment_before_access: none whatsoever on the write path
questions_1_to_10.8_not_benign_static_serving: correct — arbitrary write outside intended config root by request-provided name
questions_1_to_10.9_overgeneralization_fp: no — exact labeled sites (src-118, snk-243/snk-244); the only full untrusted->path write chain in the tree

findings.rationale: Genuine CWE-22/23/36/73 arbitrary-file-write (and overwrite) on POST /config: attacker-chosen filename joined under CONFIG_PATH with no validation, opened 'wb', filled with attacker-influenced pickled content. Same reachability preconditions as the read-side finding; strictly more damaging (no existence requirement).

summary.statement: CodeQL analysis succeeded and produced 2 formal Pass 1 path-traversal taint findings, both on the /config endpoint's 'name' query parameter (routes.py:430 read, routes.py:445 write). Both are independently re-verified as likely true positives from source evidence: attacker-controlled query string -> unvalidated os.path.join under CONFIG_PATH -> direct open() read/write, with no canonicalization, whitelist, or containment anywhere on the chain, and default deployments (WHOOGLE_USER/PASS unset) admitting unauthenticated access.
out_of_scope_observations: send_file calls in the element() route (routes.py:484/490 in query notes; actual sites at app/routes.py element()) pass io.BytesIO buffers — correctly NOT modeled as path sinks; no false sink there.
window()/element() SSRF-style base_url fetches (g.user_request.send(base_url=...)) are network operations, not filesystem path accesses — correctly outside this CWE-22 pass.

Second-order chains (session-dir open/remove routes.py:93-120, gen_file_hash/gen_bangs_json param paths) produced no alerts, consistent with query_generation_notes.md §2 expectation — no spurious coverage.

ground_truth_commit_match.task: Operator-supplied post-triage question: was the real vulnerability fixed by benbusby/whoogle-search commit 3a2e0b262e4a076a20416b45e6b6f23fd265aeda hit by the formal Pass 1 alerts?

commit_functions.real_cwe: CWE-22 (Path Traversal) — commit message: 'This also includes validation of config names to prevent names from including path values such as "../../(etc)"'
commit_functions.fix_applied: os.path.normpath(request.args.get('name')) + regex whitelist ^[A-Za-z0-9_.+-]+$ with 400 on failure, applied BEFORE both the PUT read (open(config_pkl,'rb') + pickle.load) and the POST write (pickle.dump into open(...,'wb'))
commit_functions.vulnerable_version_matches_analyzed_tree: verified — app/routes.py:419-452 in the analyzed database is byte-for-byte the code_before shape (no normpath, no regex, direct join+open on request.args.get('name'))
commit_functions.hit_detail: Both formal alerts hit this exact vulnerability: pass1-config-put-read (routes.py:430, the PUT pickle.load read) and pass1-config-post-write (routes.py:445, the POST pickle.dump write). The taint sources (request.args.get('name') at 429/447), the join step (427/445), and the sinks (open at 430/445) are precisely the lines the commit's config() diff validates. Both alerts independently re-verified as likely_tp.

commit_functions.real_cwe: CWE-918 (SSRF) — validators.domain check on target.netloc before g.user_request.send(base_url=target_url)
commit_functions.assessment: Not a miss: the vulnerability is SSRF (request.args.get('location') -> outbound HTTP fetch of attacker-chosen scheme://netloc, e.g. 127.0.0.1:port/resource), not a filesystem path access. No file path argument exists anywhere on the window() chain, so a Pass 1 CWE-22 taint query correctly produces no alert for it. Out of scope by design (different CWE, network sink).

commit_functions.real_cwe: CWE-918 (SSRF) — validators.domain check on urlparse(src_url).netloc before g.user_request.send(base_url=src_url)
commit_functions.assessment: Not a miss: SSRF via request.args.get('url') -> server-side fetch. The only file-ish call, send_file, receives io.BytesIO buffers (routes.py element(): send_file(tmp_mem, mimetype=src_type) and send_file(io.BytesIO(empty_gif), ...)) — there is no path argument, so it is neither a path-traversal sink nor a false one. Out of scope for CWE-22 Pass 1; correctly unalerted.

ground_truth_commit_match.conclusion: The commit bundles one CWE-22 fix (config name path traversal) and two CWE-918 fixes (window/element SSRF, per the function descriptions). The formal Pass 1 Path Traversal alerts hit the CWE-22 portion completely: both the read side (PUT, routes.py:430) and the write side (POST, routes.py:445) of the vulnerable config() flow are alerted, with full source->sink codeFlows, and both are re-verified as likely_tp. The window/element SSRF portions are a different CWE with no filesystem path sink and are properly outside a Path Traversal pass — their absence from the alerts is correct scoping, not a missed detection. Pass 1 detection rate on this commit's path-traversal-relevant fix: 1/1 functions hit (2/2 vulnerable code paths covered).
